mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the Federal Funds Rate above the 5-year moving average coincides with a negative 20-day S&P 500 forward return due to higher discount rates eroding expected future equity cash flows.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS crosses above its 5-week simple moving average
failure_condition: Over 60-day windows, 20-day forward returns remain positive despite rate hikes, or the 5-week SMA reverts without a sustained spike in FEDFUNDS.

mechanism_narrative: A concurrent rise in both unemployment claims (PAYEMS) and a decline in new job openings (indirect proxy via INDPRO) signals weakening labor market strength, which precedes a negative 60-day S&P 500 forward return.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases while INDPRO falls for two consecutive months
failure_condition: Over 12 months, the combined labor signal fails to precede negative 60-day returns in more than 70% of instances, or the correlation falls below -0.3.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly acceleration in home sales (HOUST) above its 12-month moving average coincides with a positive 20-day S&P 500 forward return as stronger consumer demand boosts equity valuations.
candidate_trigger: HOUST monthly growth rate exceeds +2% from the previous month
failure_condition: Across 50 such acceleration events, 20-day forward returns are not statistically higher than baseline (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in industrial production (INDPRO) of over 3% for three consecutive months predicts a negative 5-day S&P 500 forward return as it reflects contracting business capacity and reduced future earnings expectations.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO falls > 3% in three consecutive months
failure_condition: In 100 such events, the 5-day forward return is not negative in more than 65% of cases, or the IC falls below -0.2.

mechanism_narrative: When the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) prints a monthly core inflation rate above 0.3% for two consecutive months in a tightening cycle, the S&P 500 shows a positive 20-day forward return as markets anticipate rate cuts.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL monthly core inflation > 0.3% for two consecutive months and FEDFUNDS > 4.0%
failure_condition: Over 40 such inflation spikes, 20-day forward returns are not significantly higher than baseline (IC < 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in unemployment (UNRATE) below 4.5% and a rise in monthly payrolls (PAYEMS) above 200,000 indicates a strong labor market, which precedes a positive 60-day S&P 500 forward return.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE < 4.5% AND PAYEMS > 200000 for two consecutive months
failure_condition: Across 80 such labor signals, 60-day forward returns are not positive in more than 75% of cases, or the interaction IC < 0.25.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp one-time drop in retail sales ( proxy via GDPC1 quarterly change < -2% ) followed by two consecutive months of stabilization predicts a negative 20-day S&P 500 forward return as market uncertainty rises.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 quarterly change < -2% and next two quarters' change > -1%
failure_condition: In 50 such events, 20-day forward returns are not negative in more than 50% of cases, or the IC > 0.1.

mechanism_narrative: A three-month consecutive decline in manufacturing activity ( proxy via GDPC1 quarterly change < -1% each quarter ) predicts a negative 60-day S&P 500 forward return as it signals persistent supply-side weakness.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 quarterly change < -1% for three consecutive quarters
failure_condition: Over 30 such contractions, the 60-day forward return is not negative in more than 60% of cases, or the IC > -0.15.
